slides.title: Fixers do not guess
slides.text: When something breaks, good fixers follow a flowchart: a chain of yes/no questions, cheapest check first.
slides.alt: No internet on the laptop: before touching anything, build a flowchart of yes/no questions, cheapest first.

focus.cue: The ticket: no internet on the laptop

slides.title: One change at a time
slides.text: Change three things and it works? Now you do not know which change fixed it. Change one thing, then test again.
slides.alt: The printer prints nothing: the flowchart is built cheapest first: is it on, is there paper, is the job stuck, the right printer?

focus.cue: One question at a time, cheapest first

slides.title: The printer prints nothing
slides.text: Cheap, quick checks come before slow, expensive ones.
slides.alt: The printer prints nothing: the flowchart is built cheapest first: is it on, is there paper, is the job stuck, the right printer?

slides.title: The swap test
slides.text: Swap a part for one you know works. If the problem moves with the part, you found the fault. One laptop prints and another does not? Look at the one that fails.
slides.alt: The headset microphone is silent: build the flowchart, and if it is still broken, swap a part.

focus.cue: First the flowchart of quick questions

words.means: narrow a problem down to one part
trade a part for a working one to see if the fault moves
yes/no questions in order, cheapest first
turn it off and on to clear a stuck state

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Inside the Machine at Fix-It Desk and solve all 7 tickets. Build the flowchart first, with the cheapest check at the top.
